column1: # RECORD: the candidate-level lazy screen on the natural 48-candidate c4/NA19240 shortlist.
# THE RESULT IS NEGATIVE, and it is recorded rather than tuned away.
# Produced by the COARSE screen -- every fragment x candidate cell bounded at the PRODUCTION BAND
# only, no deepening -- binary md5 ab371b9c37a7f70f6553c4d648228a2c, 13.4 s on 4 threads against the
# eager oracle's 5032 s, over the same 23953 fragments and 1176 unordered diplotypes.
# WHAT THE SCREEN ELIMINATES: NOTHING. 0 of 1175 rival classes, 0 of 48 candidates.
#   coarse class width      median 728060 nats   (30.4 nats per fragment)
#   worst rival coarse upper sits 679003 nats ABOVE the best lower bound
#   per-fragment slack 28.35 nats against a per-fragment signal of 0.0578 nats
# THE SCREEN IS CORRECT, JUST USELESS. All 1176 coarse intervals contain their oracle interval
# (0 violations), and the coarse arm already names the oracle's robust leader, because the LOWER
# bounds are nearly converged at the production band -- the leader's coarse lower is only 1219 nats
# below its oracle lower, out of 1.15 million. Every bit of the failure is in the UPPER bound: the
# omitted-mass bound charges d+1 mismatches to every state beyond the production band, and at that
# band it is ~490x too loose to separate any class.
# WHY NO SCHEDULE FIXES THIS, which is why the work stops here rather than trying another ordering.
# A class {a,b} carries slack from the cells of BOTH candidates. A candidate x may be discarded only
# when every class {x, .} has U < B - tau, which needs x's partner refined too -- and x pairs with
# every candidate in the panel. So no class can be decided until essentially every candidate has
# been refined, at which point there is nothing left to save. The 800-fragment end-to-end run shows
# exactly that shape: candidates alive 48, 48, 48, then 2, with elimination arriving only in the
# final round, after the work was already spent. It finished in 182 s against the eager 195 s and
# deepened 7695 of the 7695 eligible cells -- 22283 depth increments against 22289, a 0.03% saving.
# WHAT WOULD CHANGE THE ANSWER: a tighter omitted-mass bound, not a better refinement order. This
# file is the yardstick for that -- --interval-screen-only reproduces this table in 13 s, so any
# proposed bound can be measured against these widths directly.
# NOT CLAIMED: that eager deepening is wasted work. On the analytic fixture all 1502 deepened cells
# contributed zero width to every class, but on this real panel all 7695 eligible cells contributed
# nonzero width to some contesting class. The fixture observation does not generalise.
